title: Monoidal infinity Yoneda embedding and full faithfulness on operadic diagrams
statement:
Use the quasicategories, coherent functors, mapping spaces, universes and nonsymmetric monoidal infinity categories of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'\in\mathcal U''$, and let $\mathcal C$ be a $\mathcal U'$-small monoidal infinity category; no colimits in $\mathcal C$ are assumed. Write $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$ for $\mathcal U'$-small spaces and $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'})$, formed in $\mathcal U''$. Equip this presheaf category with Day convolution: its tensor is the left Kan extension of $(F,G)\mapsto((c,d)\mapsto F(c)\times G(d))$ along $(\otimes_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$. Here left Kan extension means the functor whose maps into a target functor correspond naturally to maps from the original functor into its restriction. Then $\mathcal P(\mathcal C)$ is presentably monoidal relative to $\mathcal U'$. The Yoneda functor $j(c)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(-,c)$ has a fully faithful strong monoidal enhancement
$$j^\otimes:\mathcal C^\otimes\longrightarrow\mathcal P(\mathcal C)^\otimes$$
over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, with coherent equivalences $j(c)\otimes j(d)\simeq j(c\otimes d)$ and $j(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})\simeq\mathbf1_{\mathcal P(\mathcal C)}$. Fully faithful means equivalence on every mapping space, and strong monoidal means preserving all cocartesian edges. For every $\mathcal U'$-small simplicial set $K$ and fixed map $a:K\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, postcomposition induces a fully faithful functor
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,\mathcal C^\otimes)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,\mathcal P(\mathcal C)^\otimes).$$
Here the source and target are coherent functors with the specified composite $a$ and transformations over its identity. For any specified collection $I$ of edges of $K$ whose images under $a$ are inert, the same assertion holds on the full subcategories of functors carrying every edge of $I$ to a cocartesian edge over its inert base arrow. All these comparisons are natural under precomposition in $K$.

source.place: Proposition 4.8.1.10 with K empty and K-prime all small shapes, in the associative-monoidal case, and Variant 4.8.1.11 (printed pp.710-711); the Day-convolution description of Remark 4.8.1.13 applies with associative rather than symmetric structure. Gepner-Haugseng 1312.3178v4, proof of Theorem 5.6.6 explicitly uses this monoidal Yoneda embedding and the induced fully faithful algebra inclusion. Full faithfulness on coherent diagrams is the fully faithful postcomposition property, using the full-subcategory model of functor categories; restriction to inert-preserving objects is full. Read online; archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical theorem.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] with its small universe equal to $\mathcal U'$ and with no prescribed cocones. Its explicit localization model has no maps to invert, so it is exactly $P=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'})$, with $j$ the Yoneda functor. It is presentable relative to $\mathcal U'$. For every finite $r$, its finite-variable assertion gives an equivalence between separately $\mathcal U'$-colimit-preserving functors $P^r\to P$ and functors $\mathcal C^r\to P$, including their coherent transformations and higher simplices; for $r=0$ both sides are $P$. The presheaf categories are formed in $\mathcal U''$; for the classifying category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ in step 2 one may use an additional ambient universe containing them. This changes none of the colimit shapes, which remain $\mathcal U'$-small. In particular this use requires no colimits or preservation hypothesis on $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Example 5.3.6.4 and Proposition 5.3.6.11; agent expansion of the empty-relation case.

proof.text:
Write $m_r:\mathcal C^r\to\mathcal C$ for the operations in a unital planar operation system encoding the given monoidal category, supplied by [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. Use this normal form, including its specified pullbacks of reduced-input coherences, rather than arbitrary transformations between block functors on $\mathcal C^n$. Extend $jm_r$ by step 1 to a separately cocontinuous $M_r:P^r\to P$ with $M_rj^r\simeq jm_r$, taking $M_0=j(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})$ and $M_1=\mathrm{id}_P$. We first construct planar substitution data before adding any discarded inputs. For an $r$-input planar tree $T$, let $M_T:P^r\to P$ be the composite of its vertex operations $M_k$. It preserves colimits in every one of its $r$ variables: each external variable enters exactly one subtree at each successive vertex, and each vertex operation preserves colimits in that slot with the other arguments fixed. Nullary subtrees give fixed arguments and introduce no extra variable. Its restriction to $\mathcal C^r$ is coherently equivalent to $j m_T$, by the vertex comparisons. For every tree contraction or grafting, the original planar system gives the comparison between these restricted functors and all compatibility simplices. The full equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion], applied to the $r$ reduced variables, lifts them to the full subcategory of separately cocontinuous functors $P^r\to P$. In detail an equivalence of functor categories induces equivalences on their transformation spaces, so the homotopy fiber over each specified comparison and its already specified boundary data is contractible; one may lift entire coherent tree diagrams, not just their vertices. Grafting still has disjoint lists of variables, so both the grafted lifts and the lifts for the grafted tree belong to this same separately cocontinuous category. Their restrictions are the original grafting comparison, and the same equivalence lifts its coherent compatibilities. This constructs a unital planar operation system on $P$ and compatible coherent comparisons $M_rj^r\simeq jm_r$. For $r=0$ the restriction is the identity equivalence of $P$, so nullary compatibility is included without requiring a constant functor on $P$ to preserve empty colimits.

Only now form the block transports on $P^n$: for $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$ with opposite $a:[m]\to[n]$, the $i$th output is $M_{a(i)-a(i-1)}$ pulled back along the projection to inputs $a(i-1)+1,\ldots,a(i)$. Pull back the already constructed reduced-tree comparisons and higher simplices along exactly the projections specified in [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. Its converse gives a coherent classifying diagram and a coherent transformation from the original normal-form diagram with components $j^n$. We never lift an arbitrary transformation on $\mathcal C^n$ involving unused variables. By [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] the diagrams unstraighten to $P^\otimes$ and a cocartesian-edge-preserving $j^\otimes$; transporting across the equivalence from the original $\mathcal C^\otimes$ to its normal form gives the asserted enhancement on that original source. Inert transports are coordinate projections and the fiber at $[0]$ is terminal. For the relative inert-limit condition of [def-coef-monoidal-infinity-category], the object case of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies the mapping space over any base arrow into a tuple in $P^m$ with the product of its component mapping spaces; the component maps are composition with its inert coordinate projections. For $m=0$ this is the point. Thus this is a monoidal structure. Its tensor $M_2$ preserves small colimits separately and its unit is $j(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})$.

source.place: Agent construction using the planar projection normal form of lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence and full finite-variable completion; HA sections 4.1.2-4.1.3 and 4.8.1.3-10. Restriction is applied only before adding unused variables.

proof.text:
We identify this tensor with the stated Day convolution, including its universal transformation. For $c,d\in\mathcal C$, the map of presheaves on $\mathcal C\times\mathcal C$ with components $(u:x\to c,v:y\to d)\mapsto u\otimes v$ gives $j(c)\boxtimes j(d)\to j(c\otimes d)\circ(\otimes_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$. The mapping spaces in a product are products by the right-pinched definition, so $j(c)\boxtimes j(d)$ is the representable at $(c,d)$. By [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density], applying its evaluation assertion to $\mathcal C\times\mathcal C$, and also to $\mathcal C$, composition with this transformation induces, for every $H\in P$, an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_P(j(c\otimes d),H)\simeq H(c\otimes d)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{P(\mathcal C\times\mathcal C)}(j(c)\boxtimes j(d),H\circ(\otimes_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}).$$
The comparison is evaluation at the two identity arrows and is coherent in $c,d,H$. Here is a separate elementary deduction of the needed product-colimit fact, avoiding any monoidal-presheaf theorem. Applying [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] to the terminal category with no relations gives $\mathcal S=P(*)$ and its small colimits. The point-base case of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] identifies mapping spaces of spaces with the Kan function complex. Rearranging the factors of $T\times X\times Y\times\Delta^q$ gives, in every simplicial degree, the natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}(X\times Y,Z)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(Y,\operatorname{Fun}(X,Z))$. By [lem-coef-parametric-universal-arrows] it has the same coherent-diagram formula. If $L$ is a colimit of $Y_b$, that formula and the mapping-space colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] identify $\operatorname{Map}(X\times L,Z)$ with the space of cocones from $b\mapsto X\times Y_b$ to $Z$, via the actual legs $\mathrm{id}_X\times\lambda_b$. Hence cartesian product of spaces preserves small colimits in either variable, including the empty diagram. Functor colimits are objectwise by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Thus both $(F,G)\mapsto F\boxtimes G$ and $(F,G)\mapsto M_2(F,G)\circ(\otimes_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$ are separately cocontinuous functors to the cocomplete presheaf category $P(\mathcal C\times\mathcal C)$. Full faithfulness in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion], applied with this target, extends the displayed transformation on representables to a coherent natural transformation $\eta_{F,G}:F\boxtimes G\to M_2(F,G)\circ(\otimes_{\mathcal C})^{\mathrm{op}}$, with its specified restriction, uniquely up to contractible choice. Now write $F\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{e\in E}j(c_e)$ and $G\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{f\in J}j(d_f)$ using the small coherent density diagrams in [lem-coef-space-yoneda-density]. Use the separate product preservation just proved and objectwise presheaf colimits from [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Consequently $F\boxtimes G$ is the iterated colimit of the external products of these representables. Similarly step 2 expresses $M_2(F,G)$ as the iterated colimit of $j(c_e\otimes d_f)$. Mapping either iterated colimit into its indicated target gives the same iterated limit $\lim_{e\in E^{\mathrm{op}}}\lim_{f\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}H(c_e\otimes d_f)$, by the mapping-space colimit criterion of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. These limits exist in spaces. The displayed canonical comparison therefore remains an equivalence for all $F,G$. This comparison is composition with $\eta_{F,G}$, and the resulting equivalence of mapping spaces is natural in $F,G,H$; density presentations only test this canonical comparison and are not choices entering it. This is exactly the left Kan extension universal property in the item. For an arbitrary positive arity $r$, replace the pair $(c,d)$ by $(c_1,\ldots,c_r)$ and the external product by the $r$-fold external product. That product of representables represents the tuple, evaluation gives $H(m_r(c_1,\ldots,c_r))$, and the $r$ successive density colimits give the corresponding $r$ successive limits of these spaces. This proves the Kan universal property for $M_r$, with its comparison obtained by tensoring the $r$ input arrows. For $r=0$, the external product is the point presheaf on the terminal category; its extension along the functor selecting $\mathbf1_{\mathcal C}$ is $j(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})$, since both mapping spaces are $H(\mathbf1_{\mathcal C})$ by evaluation. For each planar tree with $r$ ordered external inputs, the canonical Kan comparison restricts to the original comparison on those $r$ representable inputs. All iterated tensors and external-product functors involved preserve colimits in all of these $r$ inputs. Thus the full finite-variable restriction equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-relative-colimit-completion] identifies the reduced-tree comparisons and higher homotopies with those constructed in step 2. When $r=0$ use its empty-variable equivalence. To pass from these active operations to a base arrow or chain of base arrows with unused inputs, pull these identified coherences back along the specified projections of [lem-coef-monoidal-block-projection-coherence]. This pullback step uses the normal-form structure, and makes no full-faithfulness claim about restriction on the larger product containing unused inputs. Consequently the arity operations, units, substitution equivalences, and coherences of the structure in step 2 have precisely the Day Kan-extension description. Thus $P^\otimes$ is the specified Day monoidal structure. By steps 1-2 it is presentably monoidal, and $j^\otimes$ has the claimed coherent tensor and unit equivalences.

source.place: HA Remark 4.8.1.13 and Example 2.2.6.17; agent Kan-adjunction/density proof. Products of spaces preserve colimits by the displayed exponential adjunction. Coherences are compared on reduced planar trees before the specified projection pullbacks.

proof.text: By [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], $j$ is fully faithful. Hence so is $j^n:\mathcal C^n\to P^n$ for every $n$: the right-pinched mapping simplicial set of a product is degreewise the product of the component mapping simplicial sets, and for $n=0$ it is a point. For objects $x$ over $[n]$, $y$ over $[m]$ and a base arrow $\alpha:[n]\to[m]$, the $K=\Delta^0$ case of [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport] identifies the homotopy fiber of the total mapping space over $\alpha$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C^\otimes_{[m]}}(\alpha_!x,y)$, and gives the same formula in $P^\otimes$. Since $j^\otimes$ preserves cocartesian edges, these formulas identify its map on these fibers with the fully faithful fiber map $j^m$, using $j^m(\alpha_!x)\simeq\alpha_!j^n(x)$. The mapping space of the base is the discrete set $\operatorname{Hom}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}([n],[m])$. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] over the identity of this base space: equivalence on every homotopy fiber proves equivalence of the total mapping spaces. Thus $j^\otimes$ is fully faithful as a functor of total infinity categories, not just on its fiber over $[1]$.

source.place: Dual of Proposition 2.4.4.2 and cocartesian mapping-space criterion; agent expansion to total mapping spaces.

proof.text: Factor $j^\otimes$ through its full replete essential image $R\subseteq P^\otimes$. By step 4 and [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image], the functor $\mathcal C^\otimes\to R$ has a coherent quasi-inverse with coherent unit and counit equivalences. These data are over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. To justify that point for the specified, rather than varying, base diagram, note that the only equivalences in $N(\Delta^{\mathrm{op}})$ are identity arrows. Project the counit to this nerve: its components must be identities, so the projected functors agree on vertices. For each edge the two triangular faces of the projected transformation give an ordinary commutative square whose vertical arrows are identities; hence its horizontal arrows agree. Every simplex of an ordinary nerve is determined by its consecutive edges, so the projected transformation is the constant transformation of a single projected functor on all simplices. Thus the inverse commutes with projection and the counit is over its identity; the same argument applies to the unit. For any fixed $a:K\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, postcomposing these inverse data gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,\mathcal C^\otimes)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,R)$. The inclusion of the latter into $\operatorname{Fun}_{/\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(K,P^\otimes)$ is a full subcategory inclusion: an $n$-simplex is a map $K\times\Delta^n\to P^\otimes$ over $a$, and it factors through $R$ precisely when all its vertices take values in $R$, by the explicit full-subcategory definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. The projection $R\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ is also a cocartesian fibration. Inner horn fillers stay in $R$ because it is full. A cocartesian lift in $P^\otimes$ from an object equivalent to $j^\otimes(x)$ ends at an object equivalent to $j^\otimes(\alpha_!x)$, so the endpoint belongs to $R$; its mapping-space pullback square remains a pullback after restricting the test objects to $R$. Thus these relative functor categories are quasicategories: they are fibers of the cocartesian exponentiation maps in [lem-coef-infinity-pointwise-cocartesian-transport], and the subcategory in question is full. Its mapping simplicial sets agree degreewise with those of the ambient relative functor category. A functor equivalence induces equivalences on mapping spaces by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Composing the equivalence with this full inclusion proves the required full faithfulness over the fixed base map $a$.

source.place: Agent proof of fully faithful postcomposition on coherent diagrams over the fixed base; uses the full essential-image model and cocartesian exponentiation.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the specified inert-labelled edges. Step 2 shows that postcomposition with $j^\otimes$ carries a functor taking these edges to cocartesian edges to another such functor. Both restrictions in the item are full subcategories on their specified objects: no condition is imposed on transformations. Therefore the mapping spaces between any two retained objects are unchanged, and the equivalences proved in step 5 restrict to these mapping spaces. Finally, every comparison in steps 5-6 is induced by postcomposition with the single functor $j^\otimes$; for a simplicial map $u:L\to K$ the equality $(j^\otimes F)u=j^\otimes(Fu)$ holds in every simplicial degree. This proves naturality under precomposition, with base map $au$ and the pulled-back specified edge condition.

source.place: Agent proof: restriction to full subcategories and degreewise associativity of precomposition.
